name: The widow of Zarephath
charge: Making the prophet's cake first, out of the last handful of meal
summary: A Gentile widow gathering two sticks to cook a last meal for herself and her son was asked by a stranger to feed him first from it, on a promise from the God of Israel. She did. The barrel of meal did not waste and the cruse of oil did not fail until the rain came, and when her son died the prophet raised him.
offense: As the Lord thy God liveth, I have not a cake, but an handful of meal in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse: and, behold, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and dress it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die. Elijah said, Fear not; go and do as thou hast said: but make me thereof a little cake first, and bring it unto me, and after make for thee and for thy son. And she went and did according to the saying of Elijah. Christ named her against Nazareth: unto none of the widows of Israel was Elias sent, save unto Sarepta.
judgment: For thus saith the Lord God of Israel, The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day that the Lord sendeth rain upon the earth. And she, and he, and her house, did eat many days. When her son fell sick and there was no breath left in him, Elijah stretched himself upon the child three times and cried unto the Lord, and the Lord heard the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived. The woman said, Now by this I know that thou art a man of God, and that the word of the Lord in thy mouth is truth.

entries.commentary: Elijah the Tishbite, of the inhabitants of Gilead, said unto Ahab that as the Lord God of Israel liveth, before whom he stands, there shall not be dew nor rain these years but according to his word. Elijah prayed and it was no rain. The teaching opens by framing the whole session on the power of the Most High: he has power over everything, the animals and all creation, and he set that power on display through his prophet.

The word of the Lord sent Elijah eastward to hide by the brook Cherith before Jordan, and there he drank of the brook and the ravens brought him bread and flesh in the morning and in the evening. This shows the power of the Most High over the animals: he can command the ravens to bring a man food if it be his will, just as he did Elijah.

The brook dried up for want of rain, and the Lord sent Elijah all the way across the land to Zarephath, which belongeth to Zidon on the coast, where he had commanded a widow woman to sustain him. From the east side by Jordan to the west by Sidon was a hard walk of a Sabbath day's journey or more, with no water anywhere. Coming to the gate, Elijah asked the widow for water and a morsel of bread, and she answered that she had but a handful of meal in a barrel and a little oil in a cruise, gathering two sticks to dress a last meal for herself and her son that they might eat it and die. Elijah told her to make him a little cake first and after that for herself and her son, for the Lord God of Israel said the barrel of meal would not waste nor the cruise of oil fail until the day the Lord sent rain. She obeyed, and she and Elijah and her house did eat many days. For trusting in the Lord and obeying, she was sustained. The instruction to feed the man of God first is a precept: the man eats first. Sisters must trust in the Lord when he tells them to reverence their husbands and be submissive in all things, and not lean to their own understanding.

After these things the widow's son fell sick, and his sickness was so sore that there was no breath left in him. She said unto Elijah, Art thou come to call my sin to remembrance and to slay my son? Her thought was that the child was paying for the parent's sins. Elijah took the child up to the loft, laid him on his own bed, and cried unto the Lord, stretching himself upon the child three times and praying that the child's soul come into him again. The Lord heard the voice of Elijah, and the soul of the child came into him again and he revived. Elijah delivered the living child to his mother, and she said, Now by this I know that thou art a man of God and that the word of the Lord in thy mouth is truth. All praises that Elijah was there to call upon the Lord, for it was not the young man's time to go. A man's days are determined and appointed, and he cannot pass the bound the Most High has set; because it was not the child's time, the Lord let his soul return.

Being full of the Holy Ghost he is led by the Spirit into the wilderness, forty days tempted of the devil, and in those days he did eat nothing. He answers with the law: man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.

The devil shows him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. No man can do that, which settles who was standing there. All this power will I give thee, for that is delivered unto me, and to whomsoever I will I give it. The offer is real, and the price is worship. Get thee behind me, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve. Again the answer is a commandment.

Set on a pinnacle of the temple and answered with scripture, he replies, It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God. When the devil had ended all the temptation, he departed from him for a season. The whole battle was fought with the word, and that is the only way it is won.

As his custom was, he went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood up for to read. He reads from Esaias: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor, to preach deliverance to the captives. This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.

They wonder at the gracious words, and then ask, Is not this Joseph's son? No prophet is accepted in his own country. He names the widow of Sarepta and Naaman the Syrian, and they are filled with wrath, thrust him out of the city, and lead him to the brow of the hill to cast him down headlong, but he passes through the midst of them.

In the synagogue there was a man which had a spirit of an unclean devil, and it cried out, I know thee who thou art; the Holy One of God. That spirit was sitting in the house of worship, and it knew exactly who he was. Knowing who he is and doing what he says are two different things.

He rebukes the fever in Simon's wife's mother and it leaves her, and he lays his hands on every one of the sick brought to him. I must preach the kingdom of God to other cities also: for therefore am I sent. He went where the people were, and some received the word and some did not.

Christ calls the twelve and gives them power against unclean spirits and to heal all manner of sickness and disease, the same works he was doing himself. The twelve are named here, ending with Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.

Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not, but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. The twelve go to the southern kingdom first, before the gospel goes to the northern kingdom.
Preach that the kingdom of heaven is at hand, heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils. Freely ye have received, freely give.
They are to carry no gold, silver or brass, no scrip, no second coat, no shoes, no staves, for the workman is worthy of his meat.
In every city they are to enquire who in it is worthy, and to let their peace rest on a worthy house and return to them from one that is not.
Where they are not received they shake off the dust of their feet, and it shall be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment than for that city.

Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves. This is a word for a people living in captivity. There is only so much that can be said and done on another man's ground, and wisdom is required alongside harmlessness.

They will be delivered up to the councils and scourged in the synagogues, which is what the Pharisees had the power to do. They are brought before governors and kings for a testimony against them and the Gentiles: against their own people who turned on Christ, and against the rulers of that time.
Take no thought how or what ye shall speak, for it shall be given you in that same hour. It is not you that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.

The brother shall deliver up the brother to death, and the father the child. Serving the Most High brings division, and it comes first inside your own house. Ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.
When they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another.
The disciple is not above his master. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, they will call them of his household worse.
There is nothing covered that shall not be revealed. What is told in darkness is to be spoken in light, and what is heard in the ear preached upon the housetops.
Fear not them which kill the body but are not able to kill the soul, but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
Not one sparrow falls to the ground without your Father, and the very hairs of your head are all numbered. That is not written for decoration; it is how closely he holds his own.
Whosoever shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father; and whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny.
I came not to send peace, but a sword. A man's foes shall be they of his own household.

He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me. This is not forbidding natural love for your family; it is forbidding the trimming of your ways to keep peace with them. That is how the pagan holidays come back in. A brother in the truth goes to see family he has not seen in a long while, and he sits down in the feast to keep them comfortable.

He that taketh not his cross and followeth after me is not worthy of me. He that findeth his life shall lose it, and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it. What is given up is the sin that was being lived in. That old man is put to death, and the life that is found is coming out of the congregation of the dead.

He that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me. Even a cup of cold water given in the name of a disciple does not lose its reward, and the reward in view is the kingdom.

verses.text: And the word of the Lord came unto him, saying,
Arise, get thee to Zarephath, which belongeth to Zidon, and dwell there: behold, I have commanded a widow woman there to sustain thee.

So he arose and went to Zarephath. And when he came to the gate of the city, behold, the widow woman was there gathering of sticks: and he called to her, and said, Fetch me, I pray thee, a little water in a vessel, that I may drink.
And as she was going to fetch it, he called to her, and said, Bring me, I pray thee, a morsel of bread in thine hand.

And she said, As the Lord thy God liveth, I have not a cake, but an handful of meal in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse: and, behold, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and dress it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die.
And Elijah said unto her, Fear not; go and do as thou hast said: but make me thereof a little cake first, and bring it unto me, and after make for thee and for thy son.
For thus saith the Lord God of Israel, The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day that the Lord sendeth rain upon the earth.
And she went and did according to the saying of Elijah: and she, and he, and her house, did eat many days.
And the barrel of meal wasted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake by Elijah.
And it came to pass after these things, that the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, fell sick; and his sickness was so sore, that there was no breath left in him.
And she said unto Elijah, What have I to do with thee, O thou man of God? art thou come unto me to call my sin to remembrance, and to slay my son?
And he said unto her, Give me thy son. And he took him out of her bosom, and carried him up into a loft, where he abode, and laid him upon his own bed.
And he cried unto the Lord, and said, O Lord my God, hast thou also brought evil upon the widow with whom I sojourn, by slaying her son?
And he stretched himself upon the child three times, and cried unto the Lord, and said, O Lord my God, I pray thee, let this child’s soul come into him again.
And the Lord heard the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived.
And Elijah took the child, and brought him down out of the chamber into the house, and delivered him unto his mother: and Elijah said, See, thy son liveth.
And the woman said to Elijah, Now by this I know that thou art a man of God, and that the word of the Lord in thy mouth is truth.
But I tell you of a truth, many widows were in Israel in the days of Elias, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months, when great famine was throughout all the land;
But unto none of them was Elias sent, save unto Sarepta, a city of Sidon, unto a woman that was a widow.
He that receiveth a prophet in the name of a prophet shall receive a prophet’s reward; and he that receiveth a righteous man in the name of a righteous man shall receive a righteous man’s reward.
And whosoever shall give to drink unto one of these little ones a cup of cold water only in the name of a disciple, verily I say unto you, he shall in no wise lose his reward.
Women received their dead raised to life again: and others were tortured, not accepting deliverance; that they might obtain a better resurrection:
